--- Page 1 (Beckerman_41a) --- Dear Jack, Yesterday we received your letter of July, and also the envelope containing the theatre programs which we will store away until you can once more pore over them yourself. We were glad to hear that your new quarters are so comfortable! No, we didn't send for that book on photography because we thought that the one we had sent earlier would contain the same information. The Jazz Book is on its way, but we had to send them your request letter that asked for it. The picture we submitted to the Bulletin was an old one that you took while here on furlough. The page with the fotos is being displayed rather prominently in quite a few stores on the avenue. We hope you won't mind the publicity. Sarah was just here with letters from Jack's mother. Jack, if we haven't written you yet, is stationed in Hawaii and so far has had no word from his picture-writers. We're the site, [illegible] about [illegible]. [illegible] very [illegible] now more - going out to draw their [illegible] --- Page 2 (Beckerman_41b) --- spirits in a little bit of the stuff. He says they succeded in getting into a happier frame of mind but swears he's not yet a confirmed drunkard! Yesterday Mama and Pepe arrived here after having spent a little week in the country. Park Ridge Manor being the official name. They had planned on staying another week for Papa had felt pretty good there - the trouble was he didn't find he couldn't get any sleep at night. He does feel a little stronger now - but is still not able to go to work. Most of the day in the country was spent in chatting with friends who were also there watching card games in progress and in between waiting for the bell to ring announcing "chow." Not much more to write today - as everything has settled down once again to ordinary routine. So Respectfully Mama, Papa
